conviction_note: The half was pre-released on 16 Sep 2026: revenue +3%, better underlying operating profit, net debt about £2m and the FY27 view unchanged against a consensus range the company published itself. The capital markets event on 25 Nov makes a guide change in this release unlikely. So the move sits on the one-session base for a pre-released period (about 3%), raised to 4.5 for thin turnover ($176k/day), a 2.3% touch spread and 44% realised vol. p_up is 48 because the reaction history leans negative (the last two interims fell 5.1% and 3.7%) and the H1 profit carries a £2.3m one-off tariff refund. The findings sum to -0.4, close to the scaled -0.18. Both are near zero for the same reason: nothing unpriced was found.

findings.finding: The stock has fallen from 247.5p on the 16 Sep trading-update close to about 218p (-12%) with no company RNS in between other than the results notice, while the FTSE AIM All-Share fell about 4%. The release will restate an in-line half and an unchanged FY view against that lower price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In-line reiterations moved the stock 0.0% (Mar 2026 trading update) and +2.6% (Jun 2026 finals). The last two interims fell 5.1% (Nov 2025) and 3.7% (Apr 2024).
findings.why_not_priced: The H1 numbers themselves are priced; they were pre-released. The only open question is whether the post-TU drift (partly an idiosyncratic -13.6% over 5-6 Oct on modest volume, with no cause in the filings) reverses on confirmation. An unexplained drawdown is worth about 0, so this is sized near 0.
findings.independence: The tape (Yahoo TUNE.L daily closes, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TUNE.L?range=3mo&interval=1d) shows the drift. Nothing independent says it reverses.

findings.finding: Liontrust Investment Partners, the largest disclosed holder at about 15%, has been a net seller through July-August 2026 (15.07% to 13.76% on 13 Jul; 15.50% to 14.99% on 21 Aug after absorbing River Global's funds). In a stock turning over about $176k a day, that is a supply overhang that is not dated to finish.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No TR-1 seen since 21 Aug. The 5-6 Oct drop on 87k and 214k shares fits a seller, but this is not established.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The holdings are public, but continued selling into a results-day bid is not visible until a further TR-1 crosses a whole-percent threshold. If the selling were fully absorbed, the stock would not sit 12% under its TU close on a flat AIM index.
findings.independence: Earlier TR-1, 13 Jul 2026: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/focusrite--tune/tr-1/9680540 (same holder, same direction)

findings.finding: Peer Roland, in its Q2 FY2026 deck (Aug 2026), flagged rising semiconductor memory prices as a cost risk that would bite more fully over time. Focusrite's H2 is its lighter half and its 16 Sep update said nothing on component costs, so any new H2 cost or margin caution would be news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin-pressure warnings have hit this name hard before (-26% Mar 2024, -15% Aug 2024 trading statements), but those were profit warnings, not caveats.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer proxy (snippet_only, deck not opened), and Focusrite has not said it applies. It reaches the price only if management raises it on the day. The company reiterated in September, which argues against a large hit, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: FiiO's April 2026 price rises citing chip costs (search snippet only). The transmission to Focusrite is unconfirmed.

findings.finding: Logitech's 27 Oct 2026 Q3 guide (sales $1.36-1.43bn, -4% to +1% y/y) sent the stock down about 12%. That is a holiday-season consumer-peripherals read-across to Focusrite's Content Creation sell-in, but the guide includes a $70-80m supplier-incident drag, so the underlying demand signal is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: A macro-to-company proxy, and Logitech's own caveat (the supplier incident) cuts against it, so it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Net debt fell to about £2m at 31 Aug 2026 (from £8.6m in Feb), so the interim dividend (prior 2.1p) has room to rise. Any capital-return signal would be new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 interims kept 2.1p and the stock fell 5.1% (on other lines).
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only. The balance sheet is public, but no capital-allocation change has been flagged, and the CMD on 25 Nov may be where any framework is set out.

baseline_tension: The lean (+0.21 from the run-up) is a weak positive and the findings sum to a weak negative (-0.4). Neither is strong: with no positioning anchor and a pre-released half, the evidence is close to balanced.

lessons_applied: Rule that a pre-released number is worth 0 and that a drawdown with no cause in the filings is worth 0: finding 1 cut from +0.5 to +0.1.
'A beat made of a one-off is sold' (H&M, tariff refund): the £2.3m tariff refund in H1 moved p_up from 50 to 48.
'Too small about the move' and thin coverage: abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5 (not to 7, because the period is pre-released and the guide is expected unchanged).
Truncated-zero rule: positioning_check states that anchor_covered is false, so there is no anchor.
